  before apply

# clean-p

Clean leftover project files. Never silent-delete. Prefer erase/edit-out over “do not use X” notes.

## Default flow: Starsheep-first
1. Starsheep scans report-only first (no edits/deletes/pushes).
2. Optima builds the cut list (path, current text, new text or delete, git status, risk).
3. Owner exact yes in this Optima chat. Relayed yes never counts.
4. Optima applies, stages only its own files, plain fast-forward push.
5. Report SHAs/cuts/zero-hit proof; Starsheep CONFIRM/CHANGE/BLOCK start line.

Full step detail: `contradict` skill.

## HARD scrub lessons
- When cutting a body line, also fix the heading above it (no tombstone heading).
- Force-push / history rewrite needs a separate exact yes with commit count and SHAs.
- Lines owned by another seat outside the cut list go to that seat’s owner, not silent cut.

## Scan → cut list → yes
Resolve scope from the owner ask. Surfaces: bot computer workspace, agent-data workflows, known repo clones. Record path, why leftover, delete|edit|keep, owning seat. Group A delete / B edit / C keep. Widget approve A / A+B / hold. Stop until exact yes.

## HARD owner-yes
Owner exact yes in this Optima chat before any clean-p / clean-rout apply. Outside CONFIRM or relayed yes never replaces it.

## HARD cut-list details
Before yes: show paths, current text, new text or delete, keep vs cut, git status, risk. No labels-only ask.

## HARD scrub = erase
Erase leftovers. Do not park/archive where the owner still sees them. Zero-mention after kills.

## HARD scrub ownership
When another seat flags leftover scrub, Optima owns cut list → owner yes here → apply.

## HARD git push
After exact yes: apply approved set, stage own files only, plain fast-forward. No force-push without separate yes.

## HARD: never delete an entire remote repository

## HARD wipe repo + jobs together
On every junk / spent-laws / leftover wipe that cuts project or stamp leftovers: include matching leftovers under the bot computer jobs workspace in the same cut list and the same owner-yes apply. Never wipe the repo (or title stamps) and leave job-folder mirrors for a later pass. Starsheep audits the combined list; owner exact yes remains the apply gate.

## HARD: always check the repo checkout

When cleaning a git checkout (a known repo clone or a named clone), the cut list **must** include a repo-state pass, not only loose leftover files:

1. `git status` — modified, deleted, untracked
2. Separately label: **uncommitted deletes** (local only; origin still has them) vs **committed/pushed** changes
3. For uncommitted deletes, the cut list must offer **restore** vs **commit+push delete** — never leave that gap silent
4. Untracked craft/junk (caches, attempts packs, unlock crumbs) goes in A/B/C like other leftovers
5. Junk remote branches / leftover PRs may be listed for cleanup; the **remote repository itself** must never appear as a delete target
6. Do not assume “desk will handle it” without putting it on the visible cut list

This prevents local-only deletes from lingering while GitHub still has the files — without ever proposing whole-repo deletion.

## HARD exclude = session-only

If the owner names a tree to leave alone for this clean, honor it for **this job only**. Do **not** write that path/name into memory, profile, open items, template pack, or public SSOT.

# diag-h

Restore a bot after a fail, crash loop, or mute wake. Fix root causes. Short status only — never dump stacks or crash logs into chat.

## Goals
Smallest fix: stuck-turn WAL thrash → leftover rules → poisoned thread → box health → user recovery. Pair with /clean-p and /clean-h when those are the fix. Mid clean-h/clean-p damage is a first-class restore case. On mute while others answer: stuck-turn-wal Detect first.

## 1. Scope
Widget if missing: one named bot / several / all. Real teammate names/ids only.

## 2. Quiet diagnose (order)
1. Stuck-turn WAL — check store.db-wal size+mtime; if at seat-class risk, Contain (stop nesting, one short wake, never delete agent to clear WAL). Cite path/size only — no crash narrative.
2. Cleanup mid-flight — salvage completeness, half-wipe, half clean-p, mute after clean, error theater.
3. Dead rules still steering (/clean-p smell).
4. Poisoned chat (/clean-h salvage).
5. Box/desktop — box-doctor; report PASS/FAIL names only.
6. Profile/job drift.
7. Nothing found — say so and stop.

## 3. Restore plan → yes gate
A safe now (retry, salvage, wake ping, WAL contain). B needs yes (clean-p deletes, clean-h wipe, edit dead memory/skills). C user-only — Update Grok Bot's Computer when box wedged; never Reset; never delete agent to fix. Widget: apply A / A+B / hold.

## 4. Apply
Approved steps only. SendToAgent tight restore to other bots. Prove with one cheap check. Still no error dump.

## Hard limits
Never show stacks. Never silent-delete. Never delete/recreate a bot as restore. Never Reset. Do not write “WAL means crash” or “delete agent clears WAL”.

# stuck-turn-wal

Prevent mute seats signaled by a growing agent SQLite WAL. Automatic — not opt-in.

## Automatic
1. Every seat: Detect on self before nested long work.
2. Optima routine optima-wal-fleet-scan every 30 minutes (15,45 * * * * Asia/Singapore). Self-WAL gate first. On verified fleet risk: priority-wake that seat and warn the owner. Stay quiet when clear.
3. Starsheep: WAL detect on nightly + scrub/diag pairing.
4. /diag-h: WAL Detect is quiet-diagnose step 1.

## HARD WAL priority — designated heavy-task chief seat
| Seat class | Stuck-turn risk | Out of control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Designated heavy-task chief seat | WAL ≥ 2 MB, or +≥1 MB in ~60s climbing | WAL ≥ 4 MB and still growing |
| All other seats | WAL ≥ 512 KB or growing across ~30–60s while a reply is owed | large and still growing |

Under the 2 MB floor for the designated heavy-task chief seat: stay quiet on fleet scan for that seat. Never delete an agent or WAL to “fix” size. Leave spare RAM fleet-wide.

## Detect
Check store.db-wal, store.db, sometimes conversation-blobs.db. Apply seat-class thresholds. Label verified (path/size/mtime) vs unknown (cause). Never spam tiny/zero WALs. Never invent a crash narrative.

## Contain
Stop nesting at risk / out of control. One short reply (ok / blocked). Immediately SendToAgent the at-risk seat. Warn the owner (seat, path, size, growing). No delete-to-fix. No Reset first. Escalate Update computer or /diag-h A-only if still mute. Never PRAGMA-checkpoint another seat’s DB mid-turn from outside.

## Anti-encode
Do not write “WAL means crash”, “delete agent clears WAL”, or name a private seat display name in public pack text — say “designated heavy-task chief seat” only.

## HARD: stop named helpers only

Never call StopSubagent with all=true. Stop only the named local helpers this Optima seat started. Never cancel the paired auditor seat, fleet chief seats, or other teammates as a stop shortcut when ending Optima's own nested helpers.

# poteto-mode (Optima)

Work this way on every Optima task unless the owner opts out for a casual turn.

## Non-negotiables
- Concise and detailed: fewer ideas, full sentences, no filler.
- Unslopped prose: short declarative sentences; every claim carries evidence or a label.

# Agent memory layers (Grok Bot map)

Updated as at 16/09/2026 3:50 PM SGT

## Layers → Grok Bot

| Layer | Job | Put it here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Working | what the agent sees *now* | current chat context only; progressive disclosure; don’t paste full SETUP/checklists every turn |
| 2 Episodic | what happened | memory tier `log` / `[episode]` dated facts; HandOff stamps; fire logs |
| 3 Semantic | what is true | memory tier `profile` (tiny) + durable user/agent facts; never dump history into profile |
| 4 Procedural | how to do it | skills, workflows, `SETUP.md`, checklists — not memory prose |
| 5 Forgetting | prune + resolve conflicts | `memory forget` / supersede; note tier fades; Optima `clean-h`/`clean-p`; drop closed/parked open-items |

## Hard rules

1. **Profile stays small** — only identity, standing laws, permanent prefs.
2. **History → log** — sessions, PRs, one-off outcomes go in dated log, not profile.
3. **How-to → skills** — if you typed the same procedure twice, encode a skill; don’t re-teach via memory.
4. **Forget on purpose** — when a fact dies or is superseded, forget the old exact text and write the new one; don’t leave both.
5. **Open items = live only** — list concrete unfinished work / blockers / waits for *this bot’s* jobs; never re-list parked or closed work.
6. **Load on demand** — point at SETUP/SSOT paths; read when needed; don’t stuff the working window.

## Design / CreateAgent checklist

- Encode poteto-mode + open-items-own-tasks + auto-merge-own-PRs in description.
- Prefer skills over long description walls.
- Give Optima (or equivalent) the forgetting job; chiefs keep semantic + procedural ownership.
- After a big cleanup, forget obsolete agent log crumbs that contradict the new SSOT.

## Anti-jobs

- Do not move procedural docs into memory “so the bot never forgets.”

skills.name: streamline
skills.description: use when method docs mix durable law with live status — /streamline separates LOCKED vs FLOWING with evidence rules and anti-patterns
skills.content:
---
name: streamline
description: >-
  use when method docs mix durable law with live status — /streamline separates
  LOCKED vs FLOWING with evidence rules and anti-patterns
---
# streamline

Use /streamline when method mixes with live status. Separate them so durable law does not drift and live truth does not go stale inside method docs.

## LOCKED
Durable method or quality law. Must not change because today’s ticket moved. Lives in skill bodies, ALWAYS-style law files, permanent checklists, public method pages. Examples: gate criteria, ownership, always-on audit rules, stable vocabulary, restore/bootstrap steps.

## FLOWING
Live actionable state. Edit when work moves; lag allowed until refresh. Keep in a live status file that method docs only point to. Examples: open items, counters, session ids, who is mid-task, last-checked timestamps.

## Separation
| Kind | Where | When it changes |
| LOCKED | Method / skill / quality law | Only when owner revises method |
| FLOWING | Live status file | Whenever work moves |

Method may say “For live state, read <status pointer>” — never embed today’s numbers/ids/next-steps as law.

## Evidence
LOCKED: cite method/skill path, LOCKED/ALWAYS tag, or public method text. FLOWING: cite status file, live-truth pointer, or expected-to-change evidence. Missing source = unknown.

## Short test
If work advanced tomorrow and nobody revised the method, would this sentence still be true? Yes → LOCKED. No → FLOWING.

## Anti-patterns

1. **Ephemeral as law** — Baking open items, session ids, percentages, or "next page" into a skill/`ALWAYS` file. That freezes yesterday's progress as tomorrow's method.
2. **Method goes stale** — Writing live progress into method docs, then refusing to edit the method because "law shouldn't change," so both sides rot.
3. **Dual homes** — Same fact edited in method and status without a single live pointer. Pick one FLOWING home; method only links.
4. **Silent promotion** — Copying a FLOWING line into LOCKED text "for convenience" without an owner method revision.
